name: LM317DCYR
title: LM317: adjustable three-terminal positive regulator, 1.25 V to 37 V, 1.5 A
summary: A three-pin positive linear regulator whose output is set between 1.25 V and 37 V by two resistors, holding 1.25 V between OUTPUT and ADJUST and delivering 1.5 A. It has internal current limiting, thermal shutdown and safe-area protection that keep working with ADJUST open. It sees only the input-output difference (up to 40 V), and with one resistor it becomes a current source. The LM317DCYR is the SOT-223 part on 2500-piece reels; parts ship with either the legacy die or a new die, and the reel label's CSO code tells which.
key_figures: 3.5 mA typ, 10 mA max at 40 V differential

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A plain adjustable supply. R1 from OUTPUT to ADJUST and the variable R2 from ADJUST to ground set the output by the output-voltage equation; the input is shown at 28 V or more. C1 is wanted only when the regulator sits more than 6 inches from the supply's filter capacitors. C2 is optional and helps the transient response.

parts.note: needed when the part is over 6 inches from the filter capacitors

circuits.title: Adjustable voltage regulator with protection diodes
circuits.description: The reference circuit. R1 and R2 set the output; the regulator holds 1.25 V across R1 and IADJ flows out of ADJUST into R2. CADJ on the adjust node raises ripple rejection. D1 lets a charged output capacitor empty into the input instead of back through the regulator, and D2 does the same for CADJ into the output. Ci bypasses the input; CO helps transient response; stability does not depend on it.

circuits.title: 0 V to 30 V regulator
circuits.description: The R1-R2 divider returns to a node fed from a −10 V supply through R3, with a diode from that node to ground. The output follows VOUT = VREF × (1 + (R2 + R3) / R1) − 10 V and runs from 0 V to 30 V from a +35 V input; without the −10 V supply and with R2 = 0 Ω the lowest output is VREF.

circuits.title: Adjustable regulator with improved ripple rejection
circuits.description: The basic adjustable circuit with 10 µF (C2) from the adjust node to ground, which steadies ADJUST and keeps input ripple off the output. D1 gives C2 a path to discharge into the output if the output is shorted. C1 bypasses the input and C3 sits on the output.

circuits.title: Precision current limiter
circuits.description: One resistor between OUTPUT and ADJUST, with the load taken from the ADJUST end, makes a two-terminal current source: the regulator drives 1.25 V across R1, so the current into the load is about 1.2 V divided by R1. R1 is a potentiometer with its wiper tied to the OUTPUT end.

parts.note: potentiometer used as a variable resistor; ILIMIT = 1.2 / R1

circuits.title: Tracking preregulator
circuits.description: Two regulators in series. U2 is an ordinary adjustable stage, R3 and the 1 kΩ R4 setting VO. U1 feeds U2's input; U1's divider runs from its output through R1 to its ADJUST and on through R2 to VO, which holds a constant voltage across U2.

circuits.title: 1.25 V to 20 V regulator with minimum program current
circuits.description: An adjustable supply with a high-value divider: 1.2 kΩ for R1 fixes the current through R1 and R2, and the 20 kΩ variable R2 sets the drop from ADJUST to ground, so a larger R2 gives a higher output, up to 20 V.

circuits.title: Battery charger
circuits.description: The divider R1, R2 sits after a 0.2 Ω series resistor RS and sets the voltage at the battery. RS limits the short-circuit output current to 1.25 V / RS and gives the charger an output impedance of RS × (1 + R2/R1).

circuits.title: 50 mA constant-current battery charger
circuits.description: The current-source connection used for a fixed trickle charge: 24 Ω from OUTPUT to ADJUST fixes the charge current at 1.25 V / 24 Ω, about 50 mA. VI has to exceed the battery voltage by at least 4.25 V, the 1.25 V reference plus 3 V of headroom.

circuits.title: Slow turn-on 15 V regulator
circuits.description: Soft start. At power-up C1 is uncharged, so the 2N2905 PNP Q1 holds ADJUST one base-emitter drop above C1 and the output starts near 1.9 V (0 V + 0.65 V + 1.25 V). As C1's voltage rises the output rises at the same rate; when it reaches the 15 V set by R1 and R2 the PNP turns off. D1 runs from the C1 node to the output.

circuits.title: AC voltage regulator
circuits.description: Two regulators back to back, one regulating each half of a sine wave: a 12 Vpp input comes out as a 6 Vpp clipped wave. Each regulator's 120 Ω and 480 Ω divider is cross-connected between the two output lines; the load is typically 2 W.
notes: Both INPUT pins take the same VI.

circuits.title: Current-limited 6 V charger
circuits.description: A 6 V charger whose battery current returns to VI− through R3. As the charge current rises, the voltage across R3 rises until the NPN Q1 sinks current from ADJUST; the ADJUST voltage and the output then fall until Q1 stops conducting. R1 and R2 set the output voltage.

circuits.title: Adjustable 4 A regulator
circuits.description: Three regulators in parallel, each feeding the output through its own 0.2 Ω resistor, with their ADJUST pins tied together. A TL084 amplifier, supplied from U3's output, takes half the output through a 5 kΩ/5 kΩ divider on its inverting input; its non-inverting input goes through 150 Ω to the 1.5 kΩ variable resistor and to the collector of a 2N2905 PNP whose base it drives and whose emitter sits on the common ADJUST node. 100 Ω joins the ADJUST node to U3's output; 200 pF runs from the amplifier output to ground. The output is set from 4.5 V to 25 V by the 1.5 kΩ resistor while the circuit delivers 4 A.

parts.note: variable; wiper tied to its ground end

circuits.title: High-current adjustable regulator
circuits.description: External pass transistors carry load current while the LM317 sets the voltage. The regulator's input is fed through 22 Ω from VI; the base of the 2N2905 PNP connects through 5 kΩ to that input node and its emitter to VI. The PNP collector drives the base of the 2N6486 NPN, whose collector is on VI and emitter on VO, with 500 Ω from that base to VO. R1 and the variable resistor on ADJUST set the output voltage, with 10 µF on the input and on ADJUST, 47 µF on the output, D1 from ADJUST to the output and a resistor from VO to ground.

parts.note: VO to ground; no value given

operation.text: An internal amplifier with a 1.25 V offset at ADJUST drives an NPN Darlington output so that OUTPUT stays 1.25 V above ADJUST. The regulator is floating: it sees only the input-output difference, so supplies of several hundred volts can be regulated as long as that difference stays within its limit and the output is not shorted. The output can be programmed as a voltage (two resistors) or as a current (one resistor), not both at once.
About 50 µA (up to 100 µA) leaves ADJUST and flows into the lower divider resistor, adding an error term IADJ × R2. The design keeps this current small and steady against line and load.
Up to 3 V between input and output is needed for full current at the lowest temperature. With less, the part drops out and the output follows the input less the dropout voltage.

The regulator's own bias current comes out of OUTPUT. If the load and divider together draw less than the minimum load current (up to 10 mA at 40 V differential), the output rises above its set value.

Current limiting, thermal shutdown and safe-area protection shut down or reduce the output stage on overload. They reset by themselves; the output is either held down or switches in and out while the fault lasts. Protection still works with ADJUST disconnected.
Pulling ADJUST to ground programs the output to 1.25 V, where most loads take little current; this gives an electronic shutdown.

No capacitors are required unless the regulator is more than 6 inches from the input filter capacitors; then an input bypass of 0.1 µF or more, of any type, is needed (a 0.1 µF or 1 µF ceramic or tantalum part is enough in most designs). An output capacitor only improves transient response. A capacitor from ADJUST to ground (10 µF in the characteristics) stops the divider multiplying ripple at higher output voltages and raises ripple rejection.

With an output capacitor, a 1N4002 diode from OUTPUT to INPUT gives that capacitor a low-impedance discharge path that bypasses the regulator. With an adjust capacitor, a diode from ADJUST to OUTPUT gives it a discharge path if the output is shorted.

Put the input bypass capacitor as close as possible to INPUT and system ground and keep the loop through capacitor, pin and ground small. At full load, use wide traces to cut IR drop and heating. Example layout: a 0.1 µF high-frequency and a 10 µF bulk bypass capacitor at INPUT, with COUT, CADJ, R1 and R2 beside the pins.

The new chip's thermal shutdown protects it, but its junction must stay at or below 125 °C. The SOT-223, TO-263 and TO-220 tabs are soldered to a board copper plane that serves as the heat sink. The SOT-223 power curve uses RθJA of 74 °C/W with 1 oz copper and 59.6 °C/W with 2 oz copper. For the TO-263 on 1 oz copper with no solder mask over the heat-sinking area, copper past 1 square inch gains little and RθJA bottoms out at 32 °C/W; its power curve assumes 35 °C/W and a 125 °C junction.
